title: Convergent prefetch and kernel synchronizer playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
This playbook describes the Convergent Prefetch + Kernel Synchronizer pattern: a coordinated runtime approach that reduces end-to-end latency for short-to-medium context LLM calls while preserving throughput and quality when kernels migrate or are evicted. The doc covers architecture, scheduler policy recipes, profiling guidance, benchmarking configurations, operational runbooks for incidents, rollout notes, and a short known-issues inventory.

Scope
- Applies to GPU-backed serving runtime processes that maintain KV caches and run multiple kernel binary variants (float32, int8/quantized, optimized-attn).
- Target workloads: interactive text-generation, chat completions, and low-to-medium token-count embedding calls with recurring prefixes.
- Not intended as a replacement for global scheduling language specifications (see scheduler-policy-language-declarative-profiles).

Goals and success metrics
- Median token latency reduction for 8–64 token responses: 10–30% vs. baseline without prefetch.
- Cache hit amplification (effective prefix reuse): +15% hit rate within 60s windows.
- No customer-visible error rate increase; failover correctness verified by automated regression tests.

Architecture overview
The pattern is composed of three cooperating components:
1) Prefetcher daemon (per-node): observes request surface and issues asynchronous KV/embedding preloads for hot prefixes.
2) Kernel Synchronizer (per-runtime process): coordinates kernel activation and safe hand-offs when model variant or kernel binary switches are required.
3) Scheduler policy adapter: exposes hints to the global scheduler (priority, warmstart score, kernel-lock-time budget).

High-level flow:
- Request arrives -> classifier tags prefix signature -> if signature is hot and predicted to recur, Prefetcher issues async KV warm request to storage layer and marks a warm hint to local Kernel Synchronizer.
- Kernel Synchronizer evaluates kernel residency and current eviction budgets and, if necessary, reserves a short kernel-lock window to finish the in-flight request using a compatible kernel variant or to trigger a lightweight warmstart of a new kernel.
- When kernel migration is required, the Synchronizer performs an in-place snapshot of kernel state (metadata + small checkpoint) and uses cooperative preemption to avoid head-of-line blocking.

Components and responsibilities
- Prefetcher
  - Input: request traces, model ID, signature hash, request frequency table
  - Output: KV preload requests (async), warm hints to scheduler, TTL metrics
  - Owner: serving-runtime/prefetch-team

- Kernel Synchronizer
  - Controls: kernel lock, safe-hand-off protocol, backstop fallback to cold model variant
  - Observability: hand-off duration, missed-handoffs, forced-fallbacks
  - Owner: kernel-and-scheduling team

- Scheduler policy adapter
  - Exposes per-request warmscore: low/medium/high
  - Converts warmscore to slot reservations and kernel affinity tags
  - Owner: runtime-scheduler team

Scheduling policies and policy recipes
We support 3 canonical policy profiles. Example YAML snippets (consumed by scheduler-control plane):

# Example policy: low-latency chat
policy_name: low-latency-chat
priority: high
warmscore_threshold: 0.7
kernel_lock_budget_ms: 30
prefetch_ttl_s: 60
max_prefetch_concurrency: 8

# Example policy: cost-conscious batch
policy_name: cost-batch
priority: medium
warmscore_threshold: 0.9
kernel_lock_budget_ms: 10
prefetch_ttl_s: 20
max_prefetch_concurrency: 64

Policy guidance:
- Keep kernel_lock_budget_ms <= 50ms for interactive workloads to avoid head-of-line blocking; raise to 100–200ms only for deterministic long-running pipelined kernels.
- Use warmscore_threshold to tune false positives: low thresholds increase prefetch cost but reduce tail latency.

Profiling and diagnostics playbook
When instrumenting the pattern, capture the following signals together in an experiment window:
- request.signature.hash
- prefetch.request.latency_ms and success boolean
- ksync.lock_time_ms, ksync.hand_off_success, ksync.fallback_triggered
- kernel.variant and model.version
- kvcache.hit before/after request

Sampling commands and quick checks:
- Start a convergent-trace: rts-trace start --tags convergent-prefetch --sample-rate 1/100
- Extract prefetch traces: rts-trace export --tag convergent-prefetch --fields signature,kvcache_hit,ksync_lock_time > prefetch-traces.csv
- GPU microprofile slice (NVIDIA Nsight CLI): nv-nsight-cu-cli --session prefetch-sample --profile-interval 100ms --target pids

Attribution checklist for root cause:
1) Confirm prefetch success rates > 95% for warmscore>=threshold.
2) Correlate ksync.lock_time spikes with tail-latency increases.
3) Verify kernel variant switch counts — high counts suggest kernel churn or model swap flapping.

Benchmarking suite guidance
Use the existing benchmarking harness (operational-workload-simulator) with the following workload templates:
- short-chat-replay: 1k users, token count 12–32, 60 RPS steady, with 20% prefix repetition (simulate session reuse).
- interactive-burst: 100 concurrent sessions, microbursts 200–400 QPS for 10s every 60s.

Suggested metrics to record in each run:
- p50/p95/p99 token latency
- kernel-handoffs per 1k requests
- prefetch cost (extra RPCs and bytes) and cost delta per 1k requests
- effective cache-hit amplification

Example benchmark config (JSON snippet):
{
  "workload": "short-chat-replay",
  "duration_s": 1800,
  "concurrency": 1000,
  "metrics": ["latency","kernel_handoffs","prefetch_rpc_count"],
  "policy": "low-latency-chat"
}

Operational runbook: incidents involving convergent prefetch or kernel synchronizer
Triage objective: restore customer median latency and stop harmful kernel churn.
1) Identify incident signature
   - Alert triggers: ksync.hand_off_success < 95% for 5m OR prefetch.rpc_errors > 1% AND p95 latency increase > 25%.
2) Short-term mitigation (5–15m)
   - Switch affected routes to policy: cost-batch (reduces prefetch pressure).
   - Disable Prefetcher for affected nodes: curl -X POST $NODE/api/prefetch/disable
   - If kernel churn causing OOMs / evictions, instruct scheduler to drain new placements with: scheduler adjust --tag affected --drain 10m
3) Mid-term recovery (15–120m)
   - Collect traces (see profiling commands) and compare last-known-good sample.
   - Increase kernel_lock_budget_ms by 10ms increments only for small cohort groups to observe effect.
4) Post-incident actions
   - Run a focused benchmark using short-chat-replay and validate p95 within 10% of baseline.
   - File a JIRA and include traces, kernel-handoff histograms, and a proposed fix.

Release notes and rollout checklist
- Feature flags: pref.kv_convergent_prefetch_v1, ksync.synchronizer_v2
- Pre-rollout tests: 1) unit tests for ksync invariants 2) e2e prefetch smoke with controlled traffic replay 3) scheduler-canary with single shard
- Canary rollout steps:
  1) Enable feature flags for internal teams and run 12h steady benchmark.
  2) Canary 5% of production traffic with warmscore_threshold conservative (0.95).
  3) Observe ksync.lock_time and prefetch rpc rate for 6h; if stable, proceed to 25%.
  4) Full rollout with staged increases to 100% over 48h.

Known issues inventory (short)
- KVCACHE-STALENESS-001: Prefetches may serve slightly stale KV entries if backing store lags during rapid model updates. Mitigation: prefetch includes model.version tag and invalidates on mismatch.
- KSYNCH-SPIN-002: Under pathological scheduler churn, synchronizer may retry lock acquisition causing CPU spin. Mitigation: exponential backoff with jitter, max retries 3.
- PREFETCH-THROTTLE-003: Prefetch load can inadvertently saturate inter-node RPC links. Mitigation: global prefetch quota per-region and auto-throttle when rpc_error_rate>0.5%.

Ownership, escalation, and related pages
- Primary owner: kernel-and-scheduling team (oncall: #kernel-rotation)
- Secondary owner: runtime-scheduler team (#scheduler-rotation)
- Security/Privacy considerations: Prefetch data must never include PII; prefetcher strips prompt content and uses signature hashes only. See security-and-compliance/risk-and-exceptions for procedures.

Appendix: quick reference tables
Policy profile quicktable:
| profile | warmscore_thresh | lock_budget_ms | prefetch_ttl_s | use-case |
| low-latency-chat | 0.7 | 30 | 60 | interactive chat |
| cost-batch | 0.9 | 10 | 20 | bulk batch inference |
| experimental-hybrid | 0.6 | 50 | 120 | latency-sensitive with high reuse |

CLI snippets
- Disable prefetcher on node:
  curl -X POST https://NODE.internal/api/prefetch/disable -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
- Inspect ksync metrics in prometheus:
  sum(rate(ksync_lock_time_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le)
